utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to everyone. We are now in session. Madam Registrar, could you kindly call the case of the current hearing.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-98-32/1-A, The Prosecutor versus Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Milan Lukic, can you hear and follow the proceedings in a language that you understand? THE APPELLANT MILAN LUKIC: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Sredoje Lukic, can you understand the proceedings in a language that you understand? THE APPELLANT SREDOJE LUKIC: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May I have may have the appearances, please, starting with the OTP. Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MONCHY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Virginie Monchy and Matthew Cross for the OTP, with Mrs. Lourdes Galicia, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I now turn to the Defence counsel for Mr. Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Dragan Ivetic, appearing on behalf of the Defence of Mr. Milan Lukic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you. And I now turn to the Defence counsel of Mr. Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon Your Honour. On behalf of the Sredoje Lukic Defence team, myself, Djuro Cepic as Defence counsel. On my left-hand side is my learned friend Mr. Jens Dieckmann, as co-counsel, and behind me is our assistant, Jacob Nuebel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This Status Conference was convened pursuant to Rule 65 bis (B) and (C) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal which requires that a Status Conference be convened within 120 days following the filing of the notice of appeal and, thereafter, within 120 days after the last Status Conference. The main purpose of a Status Conference is to give any person in custody pending appeal the possibility to raise issues in relation thereto, including the physical and mental condition of that person. This is our fifth Status Conference, as part of the appeals procedure, in the -- in the present case. The last Status Conference took place on the 11th of November, 2010. I would like to recall the parties that the Appeals Chamber is still seized of four confidential motions submitted by Mr. Milan Lukic, in which he requests to be granted a possibility to introduce additional evidence in appeal. I would also like to inform the parties that the Appeals Chamber will issue its decision on these motions before the appeals hearing. And, lastly, I am currently unable to give the parties a specific date for the appeals hearing. Nevertheless, my aim is to be able to set a hearing date towards the end of the month of May 2011, whilst taking into account the workload of the Appeals Chamber which has to manage ICTY and ICTR cases. I noted that the parties would like to be informed of the date of the hearing date and of the questions put forward by the Appeals Chamber at least six weeks in advance. However, I note that the hearing date has been somewhat postponed, which, in my view, gives extra preparation time to the parties. The Appeals Chamber will set officially the hearing date in due time and will determine the time granted to each party to present the submissions. I would like to turn to Mr. Milan Lukic now, as well as to Mr. Sredoje Lukic. I would like to ask them to inform me about their detention conditions and state of health. First of all, I would turn to Mr. Milan Lukic. Mr. Milan Lukic, do you wish to inform me about any particular detention -- any particular concerns with regard to your detention or state of health? Mr. Milan Lukic. THE APPELLANT MILAN LUKIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. As I don't know if I will be alive by the time I'm due to appear in the courtroom next time, I need to say a couple of really important things, by your leave. As for the personnel at the detention unit, everybody is acting properly. There are two professionals. I have not had a single problem in the last six years, and they have not had a single problem with me either. However, I have received confirmed information that fascists Branimir Savovic and Risto Perisic are preparing to get rid of me while in detention unit. They were the masters of life and death in Visegrad during the war. I appealed to this Court asking that they be arrested since they are criminals without precedent in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Savovic and Perisic acquired huge wealth by way of looting during the war. They have on their payroll service personnel, security personnel of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please slow down because we cannot really follow you. THE APPELLANT MILAN LUKIC: [Interpretation] Thank you. I received information that my life is in danger from the detainees who know personally Savovic and Perisic. They used to know them during the war as well. During the war, Savovic and Perisic used to work for security services and they continued to do that to this day. The security services have them under their protection. They are currently residing in Serbia, in the town of Cacak. To tell you straight away, I'm not afraid of dying. I could have been killed during the war thousands of times. I am a fighter. I always fought for justice and truth. The only battle I have before me now is to uncover the truth about the crimes committed in Visegrad against the innocent Muslim people. There were various kidnappings in Severin. Lists were drawn of innocent persons, Muslims who need to be arrested or killed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Milan Lukic, I'm sorry to interrupt you, but you do know that this is a Status Conference which has been convened in order for you to tell us about your detention conditions or your state of health. What you have just told us is not relevant for this Status Conference, but could you please conclude without too much delay. THE APPELLANT MILAN LUKIC: [Interpretation] I will continue so that everybody can conclude what this is about. There is evidence showing that the monsters Savovic and Perisic organised the kidnapping of Muslims in Strpci and Severin. There is evidence showing that Muslims who had fled Visegrad during the war were arrested on the beaches of Montenegro and sent back to the police station in Visegrad. There is evidence showing that criminal Savovic and Perisic drew lists of Muslims who need be to arrested and killed so that they could benefit themselves from it. However, those same criminals overnight turned coats and they became humanists accusing others of their crimes so that innocent people, insignificant people are rotting away in jails in Sarajevo and in The Hague while they, the actual criminals, are at liberty. I request that you order the Prosecution to ensure that these criminals stand trial, that they are arrested for the sake of the families of the victims. We ask that subpoenas be issued --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... would you please conclude now. THE APPELLANT MILAN LUKIC: [Interpretation] Very well. I request -- I am telling you that my life is in danger. I request that they be arrested. They are paying people for the killings. They are paying people to keep silent about their names. That is the main thing. My life is in danger. They committed a lot of crimes in Visegrad during the war, and they now live in Serbia. They were masters of life and death and they remain so now. So the main message is that the people who paid for murders to be committed be arrested. I have received reliable information, while in detention, that they are openly offering money for people to be killed. Their goal -- and to poison me. These are monsters. I urge you to take all measures to stop them from doing that. You need to do that only until we learn the truth. Once we learn the truth, they can be left to do what they want. There is nothing else I need to tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Milan Lukic. Of course, we all wish for you to be alive at the next Status Conference and at the Status Conference afterwards. Having said that, I take note of the -- of your concerns, but I would like to remind to you, that pursuant to Articles 81, 80 and 81 of the rules of detention, you can always put forward a request or a grievance to the commander of the detention unit or to the Registrar. Having said this, the Appeals Chamber has been seized of a motion -- or, rather, of four motions. A decision about these four motions will be delivered just before the appeals hearing. I now turn to Mr. Sredoje Lukic. Do you wish to inform me about any particular concerns with regard to your detention or your state of health? THE APPELLANT SREDOJE LUKIC: [Interpretation] Thank you for allowing me to speak, Your Honours. Everything is fine. It has been so far. I have nothing new to report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. And, lastly, I would like to ask the parties if they have at this juncture any issues which they would like to raise as we sit in this Status Conference. Starting with the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MONCHY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Very briefly, I would like to tell you that the OTP would like to talk about the disclosing of any element or any point regarding Article 98 bis [as interpreted]. I would like to say that we have recently discovered new details about the death of four [as interpreted] victims. This information have been disclosed to us according to Article 70 of the Rules of Procedure, and, therefore, we cannot communicate this to the Defence counsel before asking permission to the body who -- that give us -- that has given us this information. We have requested this to this body, and we have asked them to deal with this matter as a very urgent matter. Obviously, we will keep the Defence informed as soon as we get an answer from them. In any case, the OTP is confident that the disclosure procedure of potential exculpatory material will be completed before the appeals hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I take note of the information that you have just given us and I take note of the fact that you have -- you will give us information about this communication before the appeals hearing. Having said that, I would like to know if the Defence counsel of Mr. Milan Lukic wish to tell us anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we have nothing further to raise before the Pre-Appeals Chamber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. As far as I'm concerned, I have no other questions to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm so sorry. I'm so sorry. I now turn to Mr. Sredoje Lukic, or, rather to the Defence counsel for Mr. Sredoje Lukic. Do you wish to inform us of anything? Do you have any question to raise at this juncture?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... for this opportunity. Just for the record that we stay on our position for the oral presentation by Professor Knoops [phoen] which is authorised by Scheduling Order from 21st of July, 2010. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. As far as I'm concerned, I have no other questions to raise.

utterances.speaker: MS. MONCHY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just a slight correction to the English transcript, if I might, we're just looking for the specific line. It was said that it was about the death of four victims, but I said that we had new information about the death of six victims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Monchy. We took note of your correction and the transcript will be duly corrected. As I was saying, I have no other questions to raise, and I believe that we can now adjourn for today. I would like to thank the parties for their participation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. Problem is another mistake in transcript, page 7, line 19. My learned friend from OTP mentioned the Rule 98 bis regarding to those victims, so probably I'm not quite confident that it has to be in accordance with the truth. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MONCHY
utterances.text: Well, I don't know which line you refer to, but that should have been Rule 68. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no other questions to raise, so I believe that we can now adjourn for today. I would like to thank the parties for their participation, and I would also like to thank the staff of the Tribunal for helping us in organising this Status Conference. The hearing is adjourned.
